subject: Re: Post-call: VPC connectivity, egress & mTLS - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC connectivity, egress & mTLS - next steps

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

1) Goals we heard
- FintechCo wants private connectivity to Redwood for production inference (no public internet egress from model traffic).
- Must support IP allowlist for management plane, and mTLS for data plane between your VPC and our Private offering.
- You plan to use embeddings + reranker for semantic search in the payments product; low single-digit-second latency on typical queries is important.

2) Technical constraints you mentioned
- No outbound internet from the model VPC; all egress must go via VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint Services) or a NAT in a controlled subnet.
- Internal DNS must resolve Redwood API hostnames to private IPs (split-horizon DNS / Route53 private hosted zones).
- Procurement needs SOC2 evidence and a network diagram for security review.

3) Action items (proposed)
- I will share our VPC connectivity checklist and a reference diagram — see attached (redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf) and Drive link.
- Ben will follow up with recommended IP ranges and a sample mTLS client configuration for your infra team.
- Jonas to schedule a 30-min architecture deep-dive next week to go over SDK auth, routing policies, and embeddings/reranker best practices.

Questions for you before the call:
- Do you have a preferred PrivateLink setup (service consumer via endpoint vs our side hosting an endpoint service)?
- Which TLS mode do you prefer for client identity: mutual TLS with customer-managed certs, or Redwood-managed client certs we rotate?
- Any hard constraints on allowed outbound CIDR ranges for management-plane egress (for webhooks, monitoring, etc.)?

I'll ping a Calendly link in a follow-up so we can lock the architecture slot with Jonas.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@fintechco.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC connectivity, egress & mTLS - next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the checklist. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Preferred topology: we'd like to avoid public-facing endpoints. Our SRE prefers that Redwood expose a PrivateLink (your NLB as an endpoint service) and we create a VPC endpoint in our prod VPC. If that's not feasible, we can accept a consumer-side endpoint via AWS PrivateLink.
- mTLS: security prefers mutual TLS with customer-managed client certs tied to our internal PKI. We also need instructions for cert rotation.
- DNS: we'll need a private hosted zone that maps the Redwood service hostname to the endpoint IPs; our infra team will handle split-horizon Route53 entries once we have the IPs.
- IP allowlist: procurement wants the list of control-plane IPs and any egress IPs that your telemetry/health checks would use.

Procurement note: they need SOC2 docs and a brief summary of data flows for the security review. I attached our initial SOC questions (fintechco-soc2-questions.pdf). Also please include a rough estimate for monthly committed throughput pricing for the dedicated/private option — procurement needs to budget.

Thanks,
Alex
---
Alex Nguyen
Head of Product, FintechCo
alex.nguyen@fintechco.com | +1 (718) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC connectivity, egress & mTLS - next steps

Alex — looping in some concrete details from our infra team. Answers below + next steps.

1) Private connectivity options- Option A (recommended): Redwood exposes an AWS Network Load Balancer behind a PrivateLink endpoint service. Your team creates an interface VPC Endpoint -> private IPs resolve internally. This gives us the cleanest private path and supports mTLS for the data plane.
- DNS: once endpoint(s) are created, provide the interface endpoint private IPs; we confirm the hostnames you should map in Route53 private hosted zone.

- Option B: Consumer-side NAT/Egress: if you prefer to maintain egress through your NAT, traffic can route out to Redwood public IPs but we understand you prefer no public egress.

2) IP allowlist (management/control plane)- Management plane (webhooks, web console, and billing callbacks) uses the following ranges: 52.45.120.0/22, 34.90.200.0/24 (example; final ranges and FQDNs will be provided in HLD).
- If you need concrete /32s for firewall rules, we'll provide a minimized list during the architecture call.

3) mTLS and auth- For Private deployments we support mutual TLS with customer-managed client certs: you upload the client CA to our control plane; we validate incoming TLS client certs during the handshake.
- SDKs: the Redwood SDKs (Python/Node) accept a TLS client cert/key pair plus a ca-bundle override when using mTLS. Example client config attached (example-requests.json) and detailed steps in redwood-mtls-setup-guide.md.
- If you prefer API keys, we can issue scoped API keys for routing/quotas, but they don't satisfy your mTLS reqs.

4) Routing, structured outputs & embeddings/re-ranker notes- We'll recommend pinning your embedding model to the same model family used by the reranker to reduce cross-model latency. Jonas will demo our structured output/tool-calling patterns (function-like schema responses) in the architecture call.
- For embeddings throughput: we typically recommend batching at the client side (batch size 64-128 depending on vector dim) and use our async embeddings endpoint for large backfill.

5) Next steps- Jonas to run a 30-minute architecture deep-dive with your SRE and infra (please use the Calendly link: https://calendly.com/redwood-sre/arch-call-30m).
- I'll upload the finalized IP ranges and a one-page HLD to the Drive link before the call.
- Marissa will coordinate procurement questions and send the pricing intro.

Let us know times that work next week.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
